annotations.text:
Cut stone, chosen.

Top row: the title screen — a rail on the left, the slots as bands rather than boxes, on desktop and on a phone held sideways.

Middle row: the game itself in the same language, desktop and phone.

Bottom: the direction not taken, kept for the record.

THE PHONE, IN THE SAME THREE RULES

Flush to an edge, hairline on the inside edge only, square corners — which on a phone also buys back the twenty pixels a floating panel wastes on every side.

What moved: the readouts and the map go hard into their corners; the panel rail becomes one slab on the top edge with a hairline between each glyph; the place name is type over a gold rule, sitting under the rail rather than over the hero; the log is two bands off the left edge, above where the thumb walks.

The thumb ring is dashed here only to show where it is — in the game it appears under a finger and the corner is world at rest.

The middle of the screen is left alone. Nothing is drawn on the hero.

A · CUT STONE

Panels are flat slabs flush to a screen edge with a one-pixel hairline on the inside edge only. Square corners — the world is cut terraces.

It is the language the touch controls already use, so nothing new is invented.

B · THE TRAVELLER'S KIT — not chosen

Paper and ink, a painted signboard staked at the village edge. Kept here so the choice is on the record.

Against it: paper over sunlit grass is a harder read, and the controls have to stay dark, so it would have meant two languages.
